articles.title: Pakistan's elite want out? Khawaja Asif flags 'exit plans' of senior officers
HDFC Bank probe finds executives leaked confidential information: Report
articles.summary: HDFC Bank is conducting an internal investigation into two senior executives for sharing confidential business information. The probe began after concerns were raised about potential information leaks to outsiders. As changes in leadership approach, the bank faces mounting challenges amid recent internal disagreements. Executive transitions include Anup Bagchi becoming the new chief executive later this month. The findings of this investigation will influence future decisions and strategies at the bank.

articles.title: Mirage 2000D crashes in France, one dead; search on for missing crew member
articles.summary: A French Mirage 2000D fighter jet crashed while returning to its air base after a night training mission. The aircraft crashed near Rogeville, approximately 18 km northwest of Nancy, during its final approach. One crew member has died, while another remains missing despite ongoing search efforts by the authorities. Investigations into the cause of the accident have been initiated by local authorities.

articles.title: 'Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres': What the viral message from French protests mean
‘Was it necessary?’ Anupam Kher slams BJP minister over Daler Mehndi row
articles.summary: Anupam Kher expressed his disappointment with BJP's Uttarkhand minister Subodh Uniyal's treatment of singer Daler Mehndi on stage. During a cultural event, Uniyal called out Mehndi for allegedly lip-syncing and questioned his sobriety. Kher emphasised the importance of addressing concerns privately to maintain dignity and respect. Singer Mika Singh defended Mehndi, citing his health issues and denying alcohol consumption allegations.

articles.title: US government fines Instacart $5 million over hiring practices
articles.summary: Instacart has been fined $5 million for allegedly discriminating against US-born workers in its hiring practices. The justice department accused Instacart of creating burdens for U.S. applicants during the Permanent Labor Certification process. A settlement has been reached, requiring Instacart to establish a fund for affected applicants and pay civil penalties. The company must also revise its employment policies and train staff on anti-discrimination laws.

articles.title: Missouri court overturns ruling giving couple ownership of neighbour's road
articles.summary: In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road.

articles.title: Meloni toughens Italy protest laws: Teen detentions, parental liability, 5-year jail
articles.summary: In response to recent disturbances, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has introduced stringent security measures aimed at curbing protest-related violence. These measures entail prison sentences, fines, and even financial repercussions for parents of minors who participate in illegal protests. Authorities now have increased powers to detain youths perceived as threats, irrespective of actual criminal acts.

articles.title: Crude could hit $140 in early 2027 if Gulf supply disruptions persist: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Commodity prices are expected to experience volatility due to geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions. Energy prices may rise sharply if Middle Eastern supplies remain constrained or degrade further. Agricultural markets could face pressure from various conflicts and potential weather disruptions linked to El Niño. Goldman Sachs anticipates significant price increases for copper and gold by 2027, driven by demand trends.

articles.title: 'I try to emulate his technique': Bavuma reveals Sachin Tendulkar influence
articles.summary: Temba Bavuma has hailed the influence of batting icon Sachin Tendulkar on his batting technique after notching up a personal best of 179 runs. He emphasized the significance of movement and keeping the bat close to the body. Satisfied with his innings, especially after a rough patch, Bavuma also credited Marco Jansen and Simon Harmer for their support, urging bowlers to elevate their game as well.

articles.title: Margot Robbie's $950,000 Hollywood bungalow later sold for about $1.2m
articles.summary: In February 2018, Margot Robbie bought a charming 945-square-foot bungalow in Hollywood Heights for $950,000. After giving it a stylish makeover, she rented it out at various rates. She eventually sold the property in 2021 for around $1.2 million, marking a profitable investment. This venture underscores the appeal of smaller homes in attractive neighborhoods, complementing her extensive property collection across Los Angeles and Australia.

articles.title: Assam man earned Rs 6 a day; his farm now turns over up to Rs 80 lakh a year
articles.summary: Tileswar Handique's remarkable journey began at the age of 15, working as a daily-wage labourer in Assam. A pivotal moment during a banana sale prompted him to shift towards agriculture, where he now enjoys a successful farm generating up to Rs 80 lakh a year. Passionate about sustainability, Handique practices natural farming and nurtures traditional crops while empowering others through training sessions and exhibitions, paving the way for community growth.

articles.title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan marks 10 years in Hawaii, donates $1.48m to hospital
articles.summary: In a remarkable gesture of generosity, Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have contributed $1.48 million to the Wilcox Medical Center in Kauaʻi. This donation will be utilized to purchase a mobile MRI unit and a 3D mammography machine, reinforcing their decade-long commitment to enhancing healthcare in the community. Overall, their philanthropy has exceeded $4 million, fundamentally improving access to vital medical resources for local residents.

articles.title: Woman who revived boyfriend twice after lightning strike to get bravery award
articles.summary: During a hiking trip, Eva Broderick's quick thinking saved her boyfriend Nick's life after they were both struck by lightning. Stranded in an isolated area, they faced delays as rescuers searched for them without precise location data. After their recovery, Nick's heartfelt proposal led to their wedding nearly a year later in August. Eva's heroic actions highlight the life-saving potential of CPR knowledge in unpredictable outdoor situations.

articles.summary: Neeraj Chopra, along with his wife Himani Mor, has launched a sports management company named Vel Sports. This new venture aims to prioritise athletes' needs and enhance their performance while managing commercial commitments. The couple’s shared experiences in elite sports inform their approach to athlete representation and support. Additionally, the Neeraj Chopra Foundation focuses on developing emerging talent and improving coaching standards in India.

articles.title: ‘Dead letter box’, Rs 80,000: How 2 women supplied weapons to Tiger Shroff’s shooters
articles.summary: Investigators have reportedly found a weapons supply network in connection with the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car. Two accused allegedly traveled to Amritsar to collect firearms, sourced through a dead letter box. Anil Pandit is believed to have orchestrated these operations while compensating the accused for their involvement. The accused initially intended to target a different Bollywood celebrity before shifting to Shroff.

Missouri court dismisses widow's appeal in $220,000 trust row as too late

The issue originated from modifications to a family trust created by Violet M. Steinert and her spouse in 1994. Although Longsdon initially received money from these alterations, a court later upheld the original trust's validity.

articles.title: Ishan Kishan on the verge of three major T20 records as India take on New Zealand
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan is gearing up for an exciting five-match T20I series against New Zealand, where he stands merely seven runs shy of breaking Suryakumar Yadav's impressive record for the most T20I runs within a year. With additional matches against Sri Lanka looming ahead, Kishan is poised to chase more milestones, aiming to become the first Indian cricketer to amass 2,000 T20 runs in a single calendar year.

articles.title: Man repeatedly sent unsuitable matrimony profiles; commission orders Rs 37,000 relief
articles.summary: A consumer commission in Kerala has criticized a matrimonial agency for not fulfilling its service promises. The agency engaged in unfair trade practices, deceiving clients into buying pricier packages. In response to a complaint by Akhil Vinod, the commission mandated a refund and additional compensation. They highlighted the importance of matrimonial agencies transparently detailing their services to prevent consumer deception.

articles.title: England rugby legend Dallaglio's 2003 World Cup medal sold for £54,000
articles.summary: An exciting auction spotlighted an array of sports memorabilia, notably sounding the sale of Lawrence Dallaglio's silver-gilt medal from the 2003 Rugby World Cup, fetching £54,000. Collectors clamored for not only this remarkable piece but also his British and Irish Lions cap. Further captivating bids were made on football items, including Eric Cantona's iconic shorts and a BBC World Cup table, showcasing the rising allure of sports collectibles.

articles.title: Visually impaired Hyderabad student invents talking medicine box, wins award
articles.summary: A simple question about how visually impaired people identify their medicines led Rehan Raza to develop a device that speaks out a tablet’s name, dosage and timing, earning his project national recognition.

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines has both legs amputated after car attack
articles.summary: Helen Haines, an Australian federal lawmaker, is in critical condition following a violent car incident. Both of her legs were amputated due to severe injuries sustained during the attack. The accused driver, Brendan Nugent, has been charged but has not yet entered a plea. This incident has raised concerns about the safety of elected officials in Australia, prompting discussions on security measures.

articles.title: India moves to develop its first indigenous aviation gun for Prachand, Rudra helicopters
articles.summary: India's Defence Research and Development Organisation has shortlisted two domestic firms for developing an indigenous 20mm aviation gun. This initiative aims to increase indigenous content in the Light Combat Helicopter Prachand and Rudra helicopters. The development is expected to take around two years before production orders are distributed based on cost calculations. Additionally, efforts are ongoing to indigenise the helicopters' other weapon systems, including anti-tank guided missiles.

articles.title: Men’s jewellery beyond ceremonial gold chain & ring: Luxury’s untapped frontier
articles.summary: Men's jewellery is undergoing a transformation, transcending traditional designs and momentary trends as it emphasizes individual style and self-expression. The industry is adapting, introducing pieces that prioritize comfort and men’s unique tastes. With lab-grown diamonds enhancing accessibility, men can curate their collections over time. This shift marks a vital change where personal choice takes precedence over cultural norms, paving the way for luxury jewellery that embodies everyday significance.

articles.title: SBI data leak: Nearly 4,000 customer records found on dark web; what we know so far
articles.summary: The State Bank of India has confirmed that 3,897 customer records may have been compromised and found on the dark web. Following alerts from cybersecurity agencies, an initial investigation revealed that sensitive personal data such as mobile numbers and loan details were involved. SBI has initiated its cyber incident response plan and is actively looking into the breach's validity and origins.

articles.summary: Recent protests in France saw participants dressed as superheroes like Captain America, Batman, and Spider-Man. While demonstrations began with student grievances, they broadened to include various groups united against rising living costs. In cities like Marseille and Paris, clashes with police erupted, where costumed figures captured attention amid the unrest. Additionally, historical figures such as Napoleon were also spotted among demonstrators.

articles.title: 'Pay community dividend': Trump's message to companies building massive data centres
articles.summary: Donald Trump has proposed that large data centres should generate their own electricity and sell surplus power. He emphasized the potential for lower electricity prices through this model for local communities and the grid. Companies are encouraged to provide financial benefits to increase acceptance of data centre projects. Trump has linked the expansion of these centres to competition with China in artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Wisconsin farmer fights $900m power line that could cross 120 acres of farm
articles.summary: In western Wisconsin, rural landowners are rallying against the MariBell Transmission Project due to its anticipated negative impact on their land. The proposed route threatens family farms, with fears of diminished usable land, decreased property values, and potential health concerns. As the regulatory process moves forward, legal actions have emerged against the developers, accompanied by vigorous public protests, showcasing the strong resistance from the community of farmers and residents.

articles.title: Kaley Cuoco's 40-acre California ranch is now a refuge for rescued animals
articles.summary: In 2017, The Big Bang Theorystar Kaley Cuoco purchased a 40-acre ranch in California for $4.99 million. Nine years later, the property has become a refuge for rescued horses, cows, goats, pigs, donkeys and birds. Cuoco has transformed the ranch into a home for animals, including older ones rescued from difficult conditions, while also making it an important part of her family life.

articles.title: Chance the Rapper's charity backed Chicago youth therapy with $100,000 grant
articles.summary: Chance the Rapper's philanthropic venture, SocialWorks, has dedicated itself to bolstering mental health support for Chicago’s youth. By funding Under the Rainbow, a therapy initiative aimed at trauma-affected young individuals, SocialWorks strives to enhance access to emotional aid and nurture safe healing spaces. This initiative is part of a broader mission to uplift community well-being and empower the next generation by tackling pressing mental health issues.

articles.title: The Mecca Pact names no enemy, but why is it raising concerns in India?
articles.summary: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defense agreement on August 7, which raises security concerns for India. The agreement includes a NATO-style Article 5, meaning an attack on one is an attack on all. India is analyzing the implications of this alliance, especially due to its complex relations with Turkey and Saudi Arabia. Pakistan has deployed significant military resources to Saudi Arabia amidst ongoing regional tensions with Iran.

articles.title: 'We have plans for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': Santner sends warning to India

He emphasized the need for social justice and self-reliance as central to national development. Modi reminded attendees of the ideals of Lord Ram, focusing on justice and equal opportunities. He encouraged recognizing India's potential while serving the poor and marginalized. The Prime Minister referenced Vijayadashami as a celebration of the triumph of good over evil.

The stepson contested this ruling, alleging jury misconduct. However, the appeals court decided to uphold the initial verdict, solidifying the guardian's victory.

Crafted during Emperor Yongzheng's reign, the bowl is adorned with auspicious symbols, hinting it was a birthday gift for the emperor. After decades in the Art Institute of Chicago, the proceeds will fund new acquisitions and conservation efforts. This sale is part of a lucrative two-day auction dedicated to Chinese art.

articles.title: 1867 $5 gold coin found in Texas cigar box sells for $97,600
articles.summary: A remarkable 1867-S Liberty Half Eagle gold coin was unearthed from an obscure closet in Texas, boasting a staggering value of $97,600. After a thrilling auction, the coin found its new home in a private collection, bringing its extraordinary journey to a close.

articles.title: Women are earning, but who controls their money? India's financial literacy divide
articles.summary: In India, numerous women face challenges in making financial decisions due to insufficient access to essential financial knowledge and limited participation. Although more women are starting to utilize financial services, many still lack involvement in crucial financial decisions. This insecurity is often rooted in societal norms and traditional gender roles. Studies indicate that women who participate in financial literacy programs significantly boost their confidence and understanding.

articles.title: Air India Express flight suffers bird strike, lands safely in Bengaluru

articles.summary: Nagpur police used an e-rickshaw clue to track and arrest Shraddha Dubey and her associates. They fled from Uttar Pradesh and were located after a 24-hour surveillance operation. However, the regime's fate in Tripoli was sealed with a trick. On March 17, 2011, with Gaddafi’s forces turning their guns on rebels in Benghazi, the council voted on Resolution 1973.

articles.summary: Nishad Kumar made history by winning his second gold medal at the Asian Para Games 2026. He clinched the men's high jump T47 title with a record jump of 2.04m. This victory follows his gold in the long jump T47 event, where he achieved a best of 7.11m. Nishad's achievements make him one of only three Indians to secure two golds in a single Asian Para Games edition.

articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo was fined just €255 by Portugal’s Football Federation for walking out of the national-team camp. The modest penalty stemmed from fixed disciplinary rules, with his formal confession and clean disciplinary record reducing the applicable sanction range. Although he received the maximum fine permitted within that reduced range, his 30-day suspension was backdated, allowing him to avoid missing another scheduled international match.

articles.title: Deepika Padukone, Ranveer Singh announce name of second baby

They disclosed her name, Devi Padukone Singh, during Dussehra, sharing a heartfelt family portrait. Announcing their expanding family, they previously posted a sweet image of their first child with a pregnancy test, cleverly using evil-eye emojis to mark the joyful occasion. Their love shines brightly through this new chapter.

articles.title: No entry for vehicles below BS-VI from outside Delhi from November 1

This plan includes vehicle restrictions for non-compliant emissions and a 'No PUC, No Fuel' policy for fuel stations. Additionally, there will be limitations on construction activities to mitigate dust pollution across the city. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi is intensifying inspections at pollution hotspots and construction sites to ensure compliance.

The Martian Moons Exploration mission is designed to bring these samples back to Earth by 2031 for in-depth scientific investigation. Equipped with the Idefix rover, created in collaboration with French and German partners, the mission will conduct a 100-day exploration of Phobos.

Individuals should file applications independently and trust assistance only from recognized professionals. Recognizing fraudulent emails and suspicious offers is essential to protect against these scams.

articles.title: New York court rejects daughter’s claimed life estate in Queens property

Mary Mangiaracina had tried to secure lifetime rights to the Ridgewood property for herself and her daughter. However, after the property was sold to new owners, her daughter challenged the sale-related ownership claims in court. In April 2026, a New York appeals court ruled that the daughter had never legally received those lifetime rights.

articles.title: Watch: Masked French protesters briefly storm Marseille city hall
articles.summary: Protesters briefly occupied the lobby of Marseille city hall to voice their discontent over rising fuel costs. They shouted revolutionary slogans while some vandalized property within the building. Law enforcement later dispersed the crowd, which resulted in several violent clashes. Tens of thousands are expected to demonstrate nationwide against the increasing cost of living and perceived inequality.

articles.title: Brad Paisley and wife help open free Nashville grocery store with $1m gift

Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations.

articles.title: How Real Madrid made history with $1.42 bn in 2025-26 despite winning nothing

articles.title: Georgia renter left paralysed by falling tree gets claims revived by appeals court
articles.summary: William Frank Jennings, a Lindale, Georgia resident, became paralyzed after a tree fell on his house, despite having warned his landlord about its dangerous state. The Georgia Court of Appeals ruled that his claims against Romulus Investments were improperly dismissed, noting significant conflicting evidence regarding hazard notifications. This ruling enables Jennings to pursue his case further to potentially establish liability and seek damages for his injuries.

articles.title: 75,000-year-old Neanderthal injury may be earliest evidence of lethal spear attack
articles.summary: A Neanderthal who lived 75,000 years ago survived a severe facial injury for at least a year before suffering a possibly fatal spear wound. Researchers studying remains found in Iraq’s Shanidar Cave identified a 15mm hole in the shoulder blade, suggesting a wooden spear injury. The findings also point to possible care from other Neanderthals.

articles.title: Addison Lee founder’s London mansion once asking £32m sells for £11.5m

Disruptions to the Starlink service have highlighted the urgent need for European alternatives. Officials discussed how to strengthen Europe's satellite communication capabilities during a recent summit with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Investor interest in European satellite companies, such as Eutelsat and SES, has surged after the disruptions.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's $240 million Cowboys contract in 2024 included $231 million guaranteed
articles.summary: Dak Prescott signed a four-year, $240 million contract extension with the Dallas Cowboys in September 2024, including $231 million in total guaranteed money and an $80 million signing bonus. The deal made him the NFL’s highest-paid player by average annual value at $60 million per season. Dallas secured its franchise quarterback through 2028, betting on his leadership and passing ability to end the team’s long Super Bowl drought.

articles.title: NBA star Deandre Ayton pledges $100,000 to rebuild Jamaica after 2025 hurricane

articles.title: Tennessee man turns backyard pool into 500,000-gallon water playground

Initially a family retreat, this impressive space evolved into a gathering hub, hosting everything from birthday celebrations to weddings. Notably, it has become a venue for over 400 baptisms, deepening its community ties. Thornton's journey showcases that the pursuit of extraordinary dreams demands patience and dedication to refining one’s vision.

articles.title: UK shopper paid £1 for first-edition James Bond book; it later sold for £10,000
articles.summary: A woman bought a book at a car boot sale in Yorkshire for just £1 ten years ago. She later discovered it was a rare first edition of Casino Royale by Ian Fleming. The book retained its original dust jacket and was valued significantly. It was auctioned for £10,000, highlighting the importance of rarity and condition in collectibles. The successful bidder was a UK collector specializing in Ian Fleming editions.

articles.title: Taylor Swift gave 6,000 books to struggling library; 15 years later, it thrives

This pivotal support allowed the Reading Public Library to enrich its programs and attract thousands of community members. By 2025, the library circulated over 182,000 items and continued to foster engagement through various initiatives, proving Swift’s contribution remains vital for the region's library services to this day.

articles.title: EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
articles.summary: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.
